Rules / Modernization

SK1026 Use a UTF-8 literal for constant ASCII bytes

Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes of a constant ASCII string can use a UTF-8 literal when passed to an existing ReadOnlySpan<byte> parameter.

CategoryModernization
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floorC# 11.0
Since1.3

Why

A UTF-8 literal avoids the temporary array allocation and runtime encoding step. The consumer must already accept a read-only byte span, and speculative binding must select exactly the same constructed method after replacement. The rule does not convert APIs that need mutable arrays.

Example

Instead of:

void M() { Consume(System.Text.Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes("OK\r\n")); }

Write:

void M() { Consume("OK\r\n"u8); }

When it does not fire

Only framework Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(string), constant non-null ASCII text, and direct invocation arguments bound to ReadOnlySpan<byte> parameters are supported. Byte-array or mutable-span parameters, changed overloads, user encodings, non-ASCII text, expression trees, caller-argument-expression capture, directives and interior comments are excluded. Constant dependencies must come from metadata or this source file, including transitive initializers. Embedded ASCII escapes and NUL bytes retain their values; the literal's implicit terminator is outside the span length.
